items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: Buddy Rich used to, like there’s a tape floating around of him railing on the band.

ctx.x: How much time you got? I’ve had some embarrassing moments. The first night that the Alden-Barrett quintet worked, Chuck Wilson had to send in a sub. He had something he couldn’t get out of. And Jerry Dodgion came in and Jerry made the rehearsal, and Jerry had written a tune called “Butter” dedicated to Quentin Jackson. And I had a bunch of parts of it around, and I had like two pages of a two part, I had two copies of page one and two copies of page two and I put one and one together and taped them together and…

this band. And so we’re known going in so there’s none of this hey you guys go through the kitchen. Most of the gigs I play I’m part of the party, if I want to be, and so I don’t have that problem much anymore. And there were some gigs that I’ve been on that were misery but it’s only four hours a night max and it’s over. How bad can it be? And all gigs end. I mean it’s two weeks, three weeks somewhere and it’s over. I’ve had some problems with some temperamental people and things, and they can really get…
What’s it like working with Ruby?
